title: Molecular histomorphometry and the emerging role of transcriptomics in celiac disease diagnosis and therapeutic trials

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Molecular histomorphometry and the emerging role of transcriptomics in celiac disease diagnosis and therapeutic trials》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Aim of the review · S0001-S2004-p1】The aim of this review is to synthesize current knowledge on molecular histomorphometry and the application of transcriptomic profiling in CeD. We focus on how these approaches improve understanding of mucosal pathology, address key limitations of traditional histological assessment, and provide novel, quantitative endpoints for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. In addition, we outline practical considerations and general principles for implementing transcriptomic-based analyses in both research and clinical settings.

【Background · abstract-1-1】Celiac disease (CeD) is an autoimmune enteropathy in which diagnosis and disease monitoring rely on serology and small-intestinal histology. However, conventional histological assessment is semi-quantitative, subject to interobserver variability, and relatively insensitive to subtle mucosal changes, particularly in treated patients or during early disease. Recent advances in transcriptomic technologies have enabled detailed characterization of intestinal mucosal gene expression, revealing disease-specific molecular signatures. This review aims to synthesize current evidence on molecular histomorphometry and to evaluate the emerging role of transcriptomic profiling in improving diagnosis, disease monitoring, and therapeutic trial endpoints in CeD. In addition, we propose practical guidelines and a methodological pipeline for implementing transcriptomic analyses in this context.

【Overview of celiac disease · S0001-S2001-p3】A lifelong gluten-free diet (GFD) remains the only established treatment. However, inadvertent gluten exposure is common, and complete mucosal recovery is not universal, with quantitative histological studies demonstrating persistent injury in many patients considered clinically well controlled on a gluten-free diet [11–13].

【Overview of celiac disease · S0001-S2001-p4】Elderly people may experience a more severe nonresponsive CeD, refractory CeD (RCD) I or II with a manifest small-intestinal enteropathy not reacting to a GFD. These diseases are very rare in the general population and in diagnosed CeD patients. RCD II has a substantial risk of malignant transformation [14,15].

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:

【Conclusions · S0003-p3】Although further standardization, multicentre validation, and regulatory qualification are required, accumulating evidence suggests that molecular endpoints can complement and, in selected applications, outperform traditional histological assessments. Their value may be particularly evident in therapeutic trials, where improved sensitivity could facilitate patient stratification, endpoint assessment, and detection of treatment responses.

【Conclusions · S0003-p1】Histological assessment has served as the foundation of CeD diagnosis and therapeutic evaluation for decades, but it remains constrained by categorical scoring systems, observer variability, sampling limitations, and limited biological resolution. Advances in transcriptomics now enable quantitative characterization of mucosal injury at a molecular level, providing information that extends beyond conventional morphology.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Molecular histomorphometry and the emerging role of transcriptomics in celiac disease diagnosis and therapeutic trials》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · F0001】Figure 1. Sampling-based histomorphometry versus whole-biopsy molecular histomorphometry in celiac disease. Traditional histomorphometry relies on manual measurement of a limited number of selected crypt-villus units, typically assessing villous height, crypt depth, and IEL density. Consequently, results may be influenced by biopsy orientation, observer-dependent selection of measurement sites, and the patchy distribution of mucosal injury. In contrast, molecular histomorphometry derives a quantitative molecular injury score from transcriptomic profiling of the entire biopsy specimen. The resulting molecular signal integrates gene-expression information originating from hundreds of crypt-villus units and their associated immune and stromal compartments, thereby capturing epithelial differentiation, immune activation, and tissue remodelling across the whole tissue sample. Unlike conventional morphometry, which requires well-oriented longitudinally sectioned villi and crypts (brown vs. grey crypt-villus units) for reliable measurements, molecular histomorphometry incorporates transcriptomic information from the entire biopsy specimen, including cross-sectioned crypts and other tissue regions unsuitable for conventional morphometric evaluation. This approach provides an objective, continuous, and biologically informative measure of mucosal injury with increased sensitivity to subtle disease activity and treatment responses. Created with Biorender.com.

【Figure 2. · F0002】Figure 2. The intestinal crypt–villus axis as a model for molecular histomorphometry. Spatially organized epithelial compartments exhibit strong gene expression gradients corresponding to proliferation (crypt) and differentiation (villus) with more than 2600 genes differentially expressed [58]. In CeD, this architecture and its associated transcriptional programs are disrupted, enabling sensitive molecular quantification of mucosal injury. Created with Biorender.com.

【Figure 3. · F0003】Figure 3. Transcriptomic workflow and molecular histomorphometry in celiac disease. Upper panel: overview of a typical bulk RNA-sequencing workflow, including RNA quality assessment, read processing, alignment, quantification, normalization, and downstream analyses for cellular composition, gene networks, and biomarker discovery. Lower panel: development of molecular histomorphometry models from transcriptomic data. Expression of selected genes predicts conventional histological measures, including villous height-to-crypt depth ratio (VH:CrD) and intraepithelial lymphocyte (IEL) density, enabling quantitative molecular assessment of mucosal injury. Molecular predictions closely mirror conventional histomorphometric measurements and capture treatment-associated changes in disease activity (data adopted from Dotsenko et al. 2021 [35] and 2024[36]). See main text for methodological considerations and analytical recommendations. GFD, Gluten-free diet; PGCp, Post-gluten challenge patient treated with placebo; PGC100, Post-gluten challenge patient treated with 100mg of ZED1227 drug. Created with Biorender.com.
